name: Basilica of St. Lawrence, Asheville
architect: Rafael Guastavino with R. S. Smith
history: The Spanish architect Rafael Guastavino designed and built St. Lawrence beginning in 1905, and he is buried inside it. John Paul II raised it to a minor basilica in 1993. It is on the National Register of Historic Places and is the only basilica in western North Carolina.
arch: Spanish Renaissance Revival in brick and tile. Its dome, inspired by the basilica of Our Lady of the Forsaken in Valencia, spans 58 by 82 feet and is reputed to be the largest freestanding elliptical dome in North America.
features: Many of the stained glass windows were made in Munich.
The high altar is Tennessee marble, below a Spanish wood carving of Mary and St. John at the Crucifixion.

look.d: Built with Guastavino's thin interlocking tile, it needs no wooden frame.
Two towers frame the dome above downtown Asheville.

fun: The architect is buried in his own church.
journal: Guastavino tile above the Blue Ridge. The architect stayed with his dome forever.
